title: Three Saturdays and One Short Pan
subtitle: 度量衡 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 度量衡（人与社会·科学与技术·计量与单位）
meta: 主题语境：度量衡（人与社会·科学与技术·计量与单位）　|　核心词汇：gramme　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 gramme 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the grocer ① weighed a gramme that no customer in the shop would have described, and he said the weighing was the whole of the Saturday. The ② gramme, meaning the unit itself and not the scale, ran three Saturdays and stayed undescribed in the book; a gramme, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ gramme in that shop had the same short pan beside it, and the ④ gramme at the far counter, meaning the weight they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A gramme, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the grocer said the describing is the part that fills three Saturdays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the gramme was the whole of the matter, meaning the portion and not the unit. The ⑥ gramme, meaning the portion and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; gramme, he said, is either something you weigh or the only word that means both a unit and a portion. He said the portion is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ gramme had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short pan. The ⑧ gramme of the whole thing, the grocer wrote in November, was one shop and three Saturdays of describing; gramme, he said, is either the weight at the far counter or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ gramme I remember is the gramme described in the list, which closed in 1964 and is still described as the quietest in the shop. A ⑩ gramme, my mother said in 1966, is the only one that improves by being described; every gramme, she said, is a portion that has agreed to look like a unit. She said the portion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 克（重量单位，指店里每一克旁边的那一克）
B. n. 克（指那个单位本身，与秤相对）
C. 固定搭配：weigh a gramme 称一克
D. n. 克（指留给孩子们学着称的那一克）
E. n. 克（抽象总称，指一家铺子的称量之事）
F. n. 克（指清单里写到、被记下的那一克）
G. n. 分量；一点点（a gramme of patience，指一件事里人人都算却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 分量（抽象总称，指人人都算却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: weighed a gramme that no customer in the shop would have described
The gramme, meaning the unit itself and not the scale
the gramme at the far counter

answers.why: weigh a gramme 意为“称一克”，1958 年那位杂货店主称了店里没有一位顾客肯描述的一克。
gramme 意为“克”，指那个单位本身而不是秤，它经过了三个星期六而在簿子上没有被描述。
gramme 意为“克”，指店里每一克旁边的那一克，每一克旁边都有同一只矮矮的秤盘。
gramme 意为“克”，指最远那个柜台上留给孩子们学着称的那一克，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
gramme 意为“分量、一点点”，指一件事里人人都算却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份分量就是那件事的全部。
gramme 意为“分量”，指人人都算却无人提起的那样东西而不是那一克，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
gramme 意为“克”，指清单里写到、被记下的那一克，到 1962 年这一克成了清单里的一行。
gramme 意为“克”，店主十一月写道，整件事的称量之事是一家铺子和三个星期六的描述。
gramme 意为“克”，我记得的是清单里描述过的那一克，1964 年称完了，至今仍被说成铺子里最安静的一克。
gramme 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，一克是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的单位。
